name: Red
story: Red is used here as ink, not as an alarm. The palette treats red the way print and early computing did: iron oxide on tape and floppy media, rubricated headings, and the proofreader's red pencil on a galley. Across all three grounds the taint path (diag) is the red-pencil mark, the attack line an editor draws across the page. The red team is marking up the system, not bleeding over it. Trust boundaries use a second ink that changes with the ground: safelight amber on OXIDE, gilt on RUBRIC and blue pencil on REDLINE. On paper, red pencil plus blue pencil plus carbon type is the classic proof markup. Chip3 is always a non-photo-blue family color, the pre-press guide ink. It does the job purple's cyan does, a single cool note that keeps the page from turning into one red wash. There is no pure #FF0000 anywhere. The reds lean vermilion/cinnabar (orange side) or oxblood/madder (brown side), and the neutrals are bone and newsprint rather than white. The result reads as a printed object, not an error-state UI or a blood/danger cliché. Ground names: OXIDE (dark) is the ferric-oxide coating of magnetic tape and floppy disks, the physical substrate where bits actually lived. RUBRIC (mid) is the red-letter rubrication of manuscripts and early print, and a rubric is literally a set of rules, a nod to rules of engagement. REDLINE (light) is the galley proof that gets marked in red pencil before a run. All ratios come from a Python WCAG 2.x relative-luminance script. minor is composited over bg, and minor/major are reported but not held to a threshold, same as purple. Every text role is at least 4.88:1 and every meaningful mark at least 3.48:1. Chip separation in CIEDE2000: OXIDE 24.9 / 51.7 / 35.4, RUBRIC 25.0 / 44.6 / 32.7, REDLINE 28.7 / 45.0 / 43.6. Red against amber/ochre is the pair deuteranopes merge. Under Machado 2009 simulation every chip pair holds ΔE00 10 or more (OXIDE 10.2, RUBRIC 10.2, REDLINE 10.0, all worst-case deutan chip1-chip2). That took two lightness-only nudges of the red chip: OXIDE chip1 = diag went from #E65A40 to #E2573D, and RUBRIC chip1 from #F28A70 to #E98268. RUBRIC's taint path had been drawn in bone like the text; it now takes that red pencil too (diag = chip1, 5.47:1 on the ground), so chip1 = diag on all three grounds. The chips also differ in shape (horizontal pill, vertical pill, square) and lightness. Previews were rendered with the real build() via headless Chrome and checked visually.
